title: Chemovaccination with a late-liver-stage antimalarial induces durable immunity against malaria.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. Europe PMC record says not open access, no PMC copy, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject links, and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing. I found and downloaded the open bioRxiv preprint of the same study (10.1101/2025.07.22.666032, 433 KB of full text) and machine-scanned the whole text: zero matches for GSE/SRR/PRJNA/PXD/MSV/ArrayExpress accessions, zero for 'deposit', zero for Zenodo/figshare/Dryad, and zero 'Table S' or 'Data S' items (only 8 supplementary figures, Fig. S1-S8). The preprint's data statement reads: requests for resources and reagents go to the lead contact and reagents require a completed Materials Transfer Agreement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All biology (sterile immunity in mice up to 21 months, the CD8+ T cell antigens SERA1, RPL6, GAP50, RNT, PHIST, S20, RBP, anti-CSP antibody involvement) and all group sizes come from the preprint text alone. Group sizes quoted in the text run n=2 to n=17 mice; I could not check any underlying per-animal values because none are published. The bioRxiv supplementary-material listing page itself timed out, so the supplement contents are known only from the figure callouts in the text.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. Nothing is deposited anywhere: no repository accession in the paper, no Europe PMC data links, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit. The only availability statement is 'requests to the Lead Contact' plus a Materials Transfer Agreement for reagents, which is exactly the 'available on request' fail condition. The Science version is paywalled and has no public supplementary data tables.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (not reached, but clear). The plausible labels - whether a mouse was sterilely protected, parasite liver load by bioluminescence, antigen-specific CD8+ T cell frequencies - exist only as plotted points inside figure panels. Any feature/label table would have to be constructed by digitising graphs.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. There are no model inputs in any machine-readable form. Parasite protein sequences for the seven named antigens could be pulled from PlasmoDB, but that is a hand-built table of seven items, not data from this paper.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in the figure axes described in the text (parasitemia as percent infected red blood cells, bioluminescence in photons per second, sporozoite doses as counts, days post-infection). Not a failure point, but moot given no files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The unit of observation is one mouse. Every group size mentioned in the text is between n=2 and n=17; the whole multi-experiment study plausibly totals a few hundred animals, far under the ~400 classification minimum, and nothing like 1,500 labelled rows. Exact total unverified because no per-animal data is published.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 MB if the figure data were ever released
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size was never the problem here; mouse immunology endpoints are tiny tables.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: FAIL by impossibility: with no download there is nothing to compare the paper's counts against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance would be clean if the data existed - protection is a direct physical readout (blood-stage parasitemia after challenge), not another model's output. This is the one Part A item the study would comfortably pass.

existing_models.name: TRAP (T-cell Recognition of Antigenic Peptides), a deep-learning predictor of CD8+ T cell epitopes from peptides presented by MHC class I
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors in Genome Medicine 2023 as outperforming prior immunogenicity predictors on held-out pathogen and self-peptide sets; I did not retrieve the exact numbers, only the abstract-level claim.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Immunogenicity algorithms struggle to learn from small datasets, suffer from HLA (human leukocyte antigen) allele bias, and cannot reliably predict pathology-specific CD8+ T cell epitopes.

existing_models.name: diffRBM, a differential Restricted Boltzmann Machine transfer-learning method for antigen immunogenicity and T cell receptor specificity
existing_models.score_and_split: Published in eLife 2023; performance reported on curated epitope/TCR benchmarks. Numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Learning immunogenicity features from small amounts of sequence data remains the core limitation.

existing_models.name: EpiMatrix / JanusMatrix, rule- and matrix-based in silico epitope prediction tools applied to Plasmodium falciparum liver-stage proteins (Frontiers in Immunology 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: Proprietary (EpiVax) tools; validated by ex vivo assays that confirmed 15 novel CD8 T cell epitopes across an HLA class I panel rather than by a held-out split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which predicted epitopes are actually protective in vivo, as opposed to merely presented.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (would be the natural backbone for Plasmodium antigen sequences)
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for seven antigen sequences, which is the point - there is nothing to train on
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT licensed; irrelevant here because no labelled data exists

integration.partner_dataset: PlasmoDB / UniProt for Plasmodium berghei and P. falciparum protein sequences; IEDB (Immune Epitope Database) for known malaria T cell epitopes
integration.join_key: Gene identifier or UniProt accession for the seven named antigens (SERA1, RPL6, GAP50, RNT, PHIST, S20, RBP)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be written usefully: seven antigen names is a literature annotation, not a dataset, so joining them to PlasmoDB adds a row to a table nobody can model.

controls.positive_control: In principle the study has excellent biological controls (untreated infected mice always develop blood-stage parasitemia; anti-CD8 depletion abrogates protection), but none are usable as an ML positive control because no numeric data is released.
controls.negative_control: Isotype-control antibody and no-treatment arms exist in the experiments; not available as data.
controls.external_validation: The P. falciparum liver-merozoite experiments and the earlier WM382 chemoprophylaxis work would be a natural second source, but again only as figures in papers.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim can be written, because the study publishes no machine-readable measurements at all - only figure panels from experiments with 2 to 17 mice per group.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use parasite protein sequences to predict which malaria liver-stage antigens are recognised by protective killer T cells.
plain_idea.train_on: This was the project I considered: protein sequences of Plasmodium liver-stage antigens as input. The paper supplies seven recognised antigens by name and nothing more, so the usable example count from this paper is 7.
plain_idea.predict: Whether an antigen is targeted by protective liver-resident memory CD8+ T cells, with the true answer coming from the paper's mouse immunology assays (T cell staining and challenge-protection experiments).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Malaria vaccine developers at WEHI, Sanaria and PATH would use a reliable antigen-ranking model to pick subunit vaccine components without years of mouse work; but this paper cannot supply the training data for it.

ml_idea: Considered and discarded: rank Plasmodium liver-stage proteins by whether they are recognised by protective CD8+ T cells, using a protein language model (ESM-2) on sequences from PlasmoDB with labels from chemo-attenuation immunology. The paper contributes only seven positively-labelled antigen names and zero negatives, so any such project would be built almost entirely from IEDB (Immune Epitope Database) and other prior work, not from this paper - at which point this paper is a citation, not a dataset.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to size. Compute was never the constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement - done in one minute on the bioRxiv preprint. It says reagents on request under a Materials Transfer Agreement and names no repository; a whole-text regex for accessions returned zero hits.

verdict_reason: An excellent mouse vaccine study with no deposited data: the availability statement is 'contact the lead author' with a Materials Transfer Agreement, there are no accessions or supplementary data tables anywhere in the open preprint, and the measurements exist only as figure panels from groups of 2-17 mice. Part A1, A2, A3, A5 and A7 all fail.
